subtopics.title: Global Relations and Forums
subtopics.summary: India deepened ties with Brazil, Israel and Finland through trade, defence, technology and workforce arrangements. Brazil's state visit set a US$30 billion bilateral trade target for 2030. The Takeshima/Dokdo islets dispute between Japan and South Korea remains a sovereignty issue rooted in Japan's colonial rule over Korea.
facts: Brazil-India Strategic Partnership dates to 2006; diplomatic relations were established in 1948.
Bilateral trade target is US$30 billion by 2030; trade had reached US$15.21 billion in 2025.
India and Brazil signed a Critical Minerals MoU covering rare earths, lithium, graphite, niobium and nickel.
Embraer will set up an E175 jet assembly line with Adani Defence and Aerospace.
Validity of multiple-entry tourist and business visas was extended from 5 years to 10 years.
India and Israel upgraded ties to a Special Strategic Partnership for Peace, Innovation and Prosperity.
Israel will allow up to 50,000 Indian workers over the next 5 years.
Israel is India's 2nd largest trading partner in Asia; bilateral trade was US$3.75 billion in FY 2024-25.
Takeshima (Japan) and Dokdo (South Korea) are islets in the Sea of Japan; the 1951 San Francisco Peace Treaty did not name them explicitly.
India and Finland elevated ties to a Strategic Partnership in digitalisation and sustainability; both aim to double bilateral trade by 2030.

subtopics.title: Constitution, Law and Governance
subtopics.summary: The removal of a Chief Election Commissioner follows a special parliamentary process modelled on the removal of a Supreme Court judge, and no CEC has ever been removed. The Supreme Court recognises passive euthanasia under strict medical and judicial safeguards. Ladakh's demands for statehood and Sixth Schedule status, and the government's online takedown powers, are also in focus.
facts: Opposition parties moved a removal motion against CEC Gyanesh Kumar; no CEC has ever been removed in India.
Under Article 324(5), the CEC can be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge.
The CEC can be removed only on two grounds: proven misbehaviour and incapacity.
A removal motion needs support of 100 Lok Sabha members or 50 Rajya Sabha members to be introduced.
Both Houses must pass the motion with a majority of total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting, in the same session.
Other Election Commissioners are removed by the President on the CEC's recommendation; Parliament is not involved.
Ladakh has been a Union Territory without a legislature since 2019 and has only one Lok Sabha seat.
Ladakh demands include Sixth Schedule inclusion, full statehood, a separate Public Service Commission and two Lok Sabha seats (Leh and Kargil).
Common Cause v. Union of India (2018) legalised passive euthanasia and recognised living wills; active euthanasia remains illegal.
Section 69A allows centralised blocking of online content, while Section 79(3)(b) allows direct takedown requests via the Sahyog Portal.

subtopics.title: Public Health, Water and Environment
subtopics.summary: The Universal Immunisation Programme and Mission Indradhanush aim to protect children and pregnant women against vaccine-preventable diseases. Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 extends rural tap water coverage to December 2028 with a focus on service delivery. India's biodiversity commitments under the CBD and the Nagoya Protocol centre on benefit-sharing and national reporting.
facts: The Universal Immunisation Programme is one of the largest public immunisation programmes in the world and was re-launched in 1985.
Mission Indradhanush was launched on 25 December 2014 by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
Intensified Mission Indradhanush 2.0 (December 2019) targeted districts with 70% or below immunisation coverage.
India was certified polio-free in 2014; National Vaccination Day is observed on 16 March.
U-WIN is a digital platform to track vaccination records.
Jal Jeevan Mission was launched in 2019 under the Ministry of Jal Shakti with a standard of 55 litres per capita per day.
Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 is extended to December 2028 and aims at tap connections for all 19.36 crore rural households.
Jal Arpan introduces a formal handover protocol involving Gram Panchayats and Village Water Committees (Paani Samitis).
The Nagoya Protocol was adopted in 2010 at Nagoya (Japan) and entered into force in 2014.
Out of 23 KMGBF targets, only 2 are on track for achievement by 2030; India hosts 98 Ramsar sites.

subtopics.title: Economy, Security and Science
subtopics.summary: India's forex reserves fell by US$7.052 billion, driven by dollar strength, RBI intervention and higher crude oil prices. The PRAHAAR framework sets out seven pillars of India's zero-tolerance counter-terror doctrine. Defence and navigation updates include Mudh-Nyoma Air Force Station in eastern Ladakh and the NavIC satellite system.
facts: India opposed including the IFD Agreement in the WTO framework; it is a plurilateral agreement binding only on signatories and based on the MFN principle.
Forex reserves dropped by US$7.052 billion to US$709.759 billion; they are held by the Reserve Bank of India.
Foreign currency assets are the largest component of forex reserves, followed by gold, SDRs and the reserve tranche position.
NITI Aayog's Fiscal Health Index 2026 covers FY 2023-24 and relies on audited data from the CAG.
Odisha retained the top position among major states for the second consecutive year.
PRAHAAR is India's first comprehensive National Counter-Terrorism Policy Framework, institutionalising a zero-tolerance doctrine.
PRAHAAR's seven pillars cover prevention, responses, aggregating internal synergy, human rights, attenuating radicalisation, aligning global cooperation and recovery.
Mudh-Nyoma Air Force Station was built in 1962 at an elevation of 13,700 feet in Changthang, about 25 km from the LAC.
NavIC is India's indigenous regional navigation system developed by ISRO and needs at least 4 operational satellites.
Atomic clock failure on IRNSS-1F weakened NavIC, as functional satellites dropped from 4 to 3.

subtopics.title: History and Personalities
subtopics.summary: Shaheed Diwas recalls Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Shivaram Hari Rajguru, who were linked to the Lahore Conspiracy Case. The Dandi March of 1930 marked the formal launch of the Civil Disobedience Movement through defiance of the salt law. C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji) and the ASMITA Athletics League complete this section.
facts: Shaheed Diwas is observed on 23 March; India also observes Martyrs' Day on 30 January.
Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were executed in 1931 at the Lahore Central Jail.
Bhagat Singh founded the Naujawan Bharat Sabha in 1926; the HSRA was formed in 1928.
In the Lahore Conspiracy Case, Lala Lajpat Rai was fatally injured in a 1928 lathi charge during protest against the Simon Commission.
The Central Assembly Bombing of 1929 was carried out by Bhagat Singh with Batukeshwar Dutt.
The Dandi March started on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram and ended on 6 April 1930 at Dandi in Gujarat.
The Salt Act of 1882 gave the British colonial government exclusive control over salt production and distribution.
Rajaji was born on 10 December 1878 at Thorapalli (Tamil Nadu) and proposed the C.R. Formula in 1944.
Rajaji was the only Indian and the last Governor-General of India, serving from 1948 to 1950.
The ASMITA Athletics League was launched across 250 locations to promote women's participation in sports.

quizzes.title: Constitution and governance: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: Constitutional and legal institutions have been in the news, with several debates on how officials and courts are protected and held accountable. Opposition parties have moved to remove the sitting Chief Election Commissioner, a process set out in the Constitution that can be started in either House of Parliament. The Commissioner's position is protected by a procedure that mirrors the one used for judges of the Supreme Court. Elsewhere, the courts have been shaping end-of-life decisions. The Supreme Court has allowed the withdrawal of life support for a patient who had remained in a vegetative state for many years, applying a framework that recognises living wills and requires medical board evaluation. The judiciary also guards its own authority through the law of contempt, which covers both civil and criminal contempt and treats acts that scandalise the court as offences. In the digital sphere, the government has been reviewing how online content is blocked, while the Karnataka government has proposed restricting social media use by children. Together, these developments show how the state, the courts and the legislature continue to balance individual rights with institutional authority. Each debate raises the question of whether the existing safeguards are strong enough to protect constitutional office holders and to ensure that legal processes remain transparent, timely and open to oversight.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution is the procedure for removing the Chief Election Commissioner laid down?
questions.explanation: Article 324(5) provides that the CEC can be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge.

questions.q: How many Lok Sabha members must support a motion to remove the Chief Election Commissioner for the motion to be introduced?
questions.explanation: A removal motion needs support of 100 members in Lok Sabha or 50 members in Rajya Sabha to be introduced.

questions.q: Which Article declares every High Court in India a Court of Record?
questions.explanation: Article 215 declares every High Court a Court of Record, giving it contempt powers similar to those of the Supreme Court under Article 129.

questions.q:
Read the statements.
Assertion (A): The Supreme Court in 2018 legalised passive euthanasia in India under regulated conditions.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court held that the right to die with dignity forms part of Article 21.
Select the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: In Common Cause v. Union of India (2018), the Court ruled that the right to die with dignity is part of Article 21 and legalised passive euthanasia on that basis.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Support needed in Lok Sabha to introduce a CEC removal motion   ->   A. 100 members
II. Support needed in Rajya Sabha to introduce a CEC removal motion   ->   B. 50 members
III. Members of the inquiry committee   ->   C. Three members
IV. Effect of prorogation on a removal motion   ->   D. Motion does not lapse
questions.explanation: The motion needs 100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha members, the inquiry committee has three members, and the motion does not lapse on prorogation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about euthanasia in India:
I. Active euthanasia, through a deliberate lethal intervention, is legally permitted.
II. Passive euthanasia may involve withdrawing ventilators or artificial nutrition.
III. The 2023 modification introduced timelines for medical board decisions.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Active euthanasia is illegal in India, while the 2023 modification introduced timelines for medical boards and passive euthanasia covers withdrawal of ventilators.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner:
I. The motion can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
II. The motion lapses automatically if Parliament is prorogued.
III. Other Election Commissioners are removed by Parliament on a special majority.
IV. The Speaker or the Chairman examines the motion before admission.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and IV are correct, while II is wrong because the motion does not lapse on prorogation and III is wrong because the President removes other ECs.

questions.q: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, violations of its child-protection provisions may attract penalties up to what amount?
questions.explanation: The text states that violations may attract financial penalties up to 200 crore under the DPDP Act's provisions on children.

quizzes.title: History and personalities: typed answer practice
quizzes.passage: Several episodes of India's freedom struggle were recalled in recent public events, highlighting the sacrifices of young revolutionaries and national leaders. Shaheed Diwas is observed every year to honour Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev Thapar and Shivaram Hari Rajguru, who were executed in the Lahore Central Jail. Their activities were linked to the Lahore Conspiracy Case, which followed the fatal injury of Lala Lajpat Rai during a protest against the Simon Commission. Mahatma Gandhi's protest against the colonial salt monopoly is another landmark. He led a march from the Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad to the coastal village of Dandi in Gujarat, where he produced salt from seawater to defy the salt law. The march was triggered after the Viceroy rejected Gandhi's eleven-point demands, which included the abolition of the salt tax. Chakravarti Rajagopalachari, popularly known as Rajaji, was another key figure of this era. He led the Vedaranyam salt march in South India and later proposed a compromise formula to prevent the partition of the country. After independence he served as Governor-General, and he later founded the Swatantra Party. In sports, the government launched a nationwide grassroots athletics league to encourage women's participation. The league is linked to the Khelo India scheme and aims to identify talent from rural, tribal and school levels across age groups.

questions.q: In which year did the Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) begin? (year)
questions.explanation: The march began on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram.

questions.q: On which day of March is Shaheed Diwas observed? (day of the month)
questions.explanation: Shaheed Diwas is observed on 23 March.

questions.q: In which year did the British colonial government enact the Salt Act? (year)
questions.explanation: The Salt Act of 1882 gave the British exclusive control over salt production and distribution.

questions.q: Which Viceroy of India rejected Gandhi's eleven-point demands before the Dandi March? (surname)
questions.explanation: Lord Irwin, the Viceroy of India, rejected the 11-point demands, which triggered the march.

questions.q: In which year did C. Rajagopalachari propose the C.R. Formula? (year)
questions.explanation: Rajaji proposed the C.R. Formula in 1944 as a compromise to resolve the political deadlock between the Congress and the Muslim League.

questions.q: In which Indian state is Thorapalli, the birthplace of Rajaji, located? (name of state)
questions.explanation: Rajaji was born on 10 December 1878 at Thorapalli in Tamil Nadu.

questions.q: Across how many locations was the ASMITA Athletics League launched? (number)
questions.explanation: The Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports launched the ASMITA Athletics League across 250 locations.
